source_quote: Athletic breed groups exhibited moderate hip dysplasia prevalence across North American screening data.
Sporting and working breed dogs showed elevated cranial cruciate ligament rupture incidence.
Heavy-framed and large-breed dogs were overrepresented in osteoarthritis diagnoses.
Large heavy-framed breeds showed elevated hip dysplasia prevalence in radiographic screening.
Chondrodystrophic breeds demonstrated markedly elevated intervertebral disc disease prevalence.
Small limb-disproportionate breeds showed increased patellar instability risk.
Compact brachycephalic skull conformation correlated with chronic upper airway burden.
Compact skull morphology and jaw crowding increased periodontal disease prevalence.
Deep thoracic conformation remained a major gastric dilatation-volvulus risk factor.
Deep-chested large breed morphology was enriched in dilated cardiomyopathy diagnoses.
